# test_validate_password.py
import pytest

# If validate_password is defined in another module (e.g. mymodule.py) you would do
#     from mymodule import validate_password
# For the snippet given, we assume it is available on the import path.
from validate_password import validate_password   # adjust to your project structure


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happy-path tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "password",
    [
        "Abcdef12",        # simple mixture, > 8 chars
        "A1b2c3d4e5",      # long, alternating character classes
        "PASSword9!",      # special char is allowed
        "StrongPass1",     # typical strong password
        "Aa1aaaaa",        # exactly 8 characters (edge of valid length)
    ],
)
def test_validate_password_happy_path(password):
    """Passwords that fulfill every rule must be accepted."""
    assert validate_password(password) is True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Length-based edge cases
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "password, expected",
    [
        ("A1b2c3d", False),      # 7 chars -> too short
        ("", False),             # empty string
        ("Aa1aaaaa", True),      # exactly 8 chars (already covered above but explicit here)
    ],
)
def test_validate_password_length_requirement(password, expected):
    assert validate_password(password) is expected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Character-class edge cases
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "password, expected_reason",
    [
        ("abcdefg1", "no uppercase"),
        ("ABCDEFG1", "no lowercase"),
        ("Abcdefgh", "no digit"),
    ],
)
def test_validate_password_missing_character_class(password, expected_reason):
    """Each mandatory character class must be present."""
    assert validate_password(password) is False, f"Should fail because {expected_reason}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error / exceptional cases
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_input", [None, 123, 3.14])
def test_validate_password_non_string_raises_type_error(bad_input):
    """
    validate_password is specified to accept `str`.  
    Passing a non-string should propagate the TypeError coming from `len()`.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        validate_password(bad_input)
